root_cause.text: The netfilter conntrack netlink interface lacked bounds/range validation in its nla_policy for user-controlled SCTP state and expectation NAT direction attributes, allowing invalid values to be written into conntrack state and later used as array indexes.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states these attributes were "used by the kernel without any validation"; specifically, "nlattr_to_sctp() assigns the user-supplied CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE value directly to ct->proto.sctp.state without checking that it is within the valid range" and "with exp->dir = 100, the access at ct->master->tuplehash[100] reads 5600 bytes past"; the patch fixes this by changing CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., IP_CT_DIR_REPLY)` and CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT)`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The netfilter conntrack netlink interface lacked bounds/range validation in its nla_policy for user-controlled SCTP state and expectation NAT direction attributes, allowing invalid values to be written into conntrack state and later used as array indexes.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states these attributes were "used by the kernel without any validation"; specifically, "nlattr_to_sctp() assigns the user-supplied CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE value directly to ct->proto.sctp.state without checking that it is within the valid range" and "with exp->dir = 100, the access at ct->master->tuplehash[100] reads 5600 bytes past"; the patch fixes this by changing CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., IP_CT_DIR_REPLY)` and CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(..., SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR as a bounded big-endian direction value so invalid netlink NAT expectation directions are rejected.
intent_record.what: The netlink attribute policy for CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR in exp_nat_nla_policy was changed from a plain .type = NLA_U32 entry to NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_BE32, IP_CT_DIR_REPLY), adding a maximum-value constrained policy and changing the expected attribute type to big-endian 32-bit.
intent_record.how: At runtime, netlink validation now enforces that CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR is encoded as a big-endian 32-bit value and rejects values greater than IP_CT_DIR_REPLY, preventing invalid direction values from being accepted for expectation NAT configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add range validation for the SCTP netlink state attribute so only valid conntrack state values are accepted.
intent_record.what: The netlink attribute policy entry for CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE was changed from a plain NLA_U8 type declaration to an NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT) policy, adding an explicit maximum allowed value for the SCTP state attribute.
intent_record.how: At runtime, netlink validation will now reject CTA_PROTOINFO_SCTP_STATE values greater than SCTP_CONNTRACK_HEARTBEAT_SENT instead of accepting any 8-bit value, preventing invalid SCTP conntrack state values from being parsed or applied.

grouping_result.intent: Add range validation for the SCTP netlink state attribute so only valid conntrack state values are accepted.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add netlink attribute range validation to reject invalid conntrack-related enum/direction values before they are accepted by the kernel.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly add missing netlink bounds/range validation for the exact user-controlled attributes in the root cause: expectation NAT direction and SCTP state, preventing invalid values from being accepted and later used as array indexes.

candidates.rationale: This policy accepted any 32-bit value for CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR without constraining it to valid direction enum values, allowing user-controlled invalid directions to be stored and later used unsafely.
This policy accepted any 8-bit SCTP state value without validating it against the valid conntrack SCTP state range, enabling invalid state values to be written and later used as array indexes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This nla_policy entry accepted any 32-bit user-supplied CTA_EXPECT_NAT_DIR value without restricting it to valid direction enum values, matching the root cause of missing bounds validation before later unsafe use as an index-related state/direction value.

This nla_policy entry accepted any 8-bit user-controlled SCTP state without range checking against valid SCTP conntrack states, enabling invalid state values to be stored and later used as array indexes.
